target_customer: Online sellers and small e-commerce merchants in the Philippines
problem: Merchants book deliveries manually across several couriers, which is slow and makes rate comparison hard.
business_model: Per order booking fee on a multi courier shipping aggregator (30 cents per order per TechCrunch)

founders.name: Josh Supan
founders.background_notes: YC page lists no background. TechNode says he and Marquez started Shipmates in July 2021.

founders.name: David Marquez
founders.background_notes: No background on the YC page.

competitors.name: Ninja Van Philippines
competitors.what: Courier with its own network and a multi carrier shipping offering for sellers
competitors.traction_then: Company states parcel volumes grew 150 percent from 2020 to 2021

competitors.name: Lalamove
competitors.what: On demand courier, also a Shipmates partner rather than a pure rival

technical_complexity.rationale: Courier API integrations, Shopify connector and booking flows; mostly integration work.

defensibility.rationale: Couriers could add multi carrier features themselves, and integrations are copyable; value rests on execution and partner relationships.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not determined. The company's own site at shipmates.app showed Service Discontinued when fetched in November 2026, but no press about a shutdown was found.

market_need_then: E-commerce boom in the Philippines during the pandemic, with fragmented couriers and cash on delivery needs for small sellers.

identity.voice_and_tone: Simple and merchant friendly: simplify logistics, simplicity in design

branding.community_and_virality: Coverage of its seed round in TechCrunch, DealStreetAsia, Philstar and a podcast interview; no brand community found.

brand_strength.rationale: A friendly compound name but generic and shared with several unrelated Shipmates products; brand press was about the funding, not the brand.

outcome_analysis: Shipmates launched a beta in August 2021, joined YC in Summer 2022 and raised a 2.2 million dollar seed in September 2022 from regional investors. Its website now shows service discontinued, while the YC directory lists it as active and no shutdown reporting was found, so the cause and timing of any wind down are not public. The aggregator model faced courier networks that could offer similar tools.
notes: Seed 2.2M (P125M) stated by TechNode and Philstar headline (also DealStreetAsia, Malaya). Investor lists conflict: TechNode names Cathexis, Wavemaker, Taurus, Capital X and Sketchnote; another source names Unpopular Ventures and Amino Capital. TechNode says YC gave 500K earlier (not recorded as a round). Aggregators list 2.3M to 3.1M totals, unverified. Status conflict: YC lists Active but the company site title read Service Discontinued; I did not find a source explaining it, so exit type is unknown. Competitor sources are undated vendor pages; Ninja Van is dated only by its 2020 to 2021 growth claim. A 2017 e-commerce enabler earlier startup comes from a single search summary and is omitted.
